overall_diagnosis: All three samples agree: the task fails only on test_value_magnitudes because Ystar_base lands at ~78 instead of the expected 10,000–500,000 range. Root cause is a unit mismatch between PWT capital stock (millions of 2017 USD) and WEO real GDP (local-currency GEL at a different scale) when applying the Cobb-Douglas identity Y* = exp(lnZ_trend) * K^alpha. The HP-filtered lnZ absorbed the mismatch over history, but the forward reconstruction then produced the wrong scale. The xlsx skill is the only inventory item and currently lacks concrete, task-anchored guidance on reconciling multi-source macro data units and sanity-checking output magnitudes. A prior patch was rejected for not moving the needle — the next attempt must be more concrete and actionable (named conversion cell, explicit numeric sanity threshold tied to the Y_observed anchor, and worked PWT↔WEO reconciliation example for Georgia).

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The xlsx skill addresses formula hygiene, color coding, and header unit labels but gives no operational procedure for reconciling multi-source macro inputs (PWT capital in mn 2017 USD vs WEO real GDP in local currency) nor a mandatory magnitude sanity check on reconstructed series. For shock-analysis-supply this caused Ystar_base ≈ 78 instead of ~78,000 (mn GEL), failing test_value_magnitudes while all structural tests passed. The earlier patch was rejected (no improvement), so the repair must be sharper: a short, concrete, task-anchored procedure with named cells, an explicit numeric tolerance, and a worked Georgia PWT→GEL conversion example — not just general advice.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Rewrite the skill to add a tight, concrete 'Multi-Source Macro Unit Reconciliation' section with these mandatory steps (keep it short and actionable, not generic): (1) In every input block, add a single named conversion cell (blue font, yellow highlight) e.g. `K_unit_conv` with a comment citing source and value — for Georgia convert PWT `rnna` from mn 2017 USD to mn GEL using the 2017 average USD/GEL rate ≈ 2.51 (or document use of PWT PPP series), and build `K_GEL = rnna * K_unit_conv`. (2) Use the SAME K series (same units) both when deriving lnZ = lnY − α·lnK AND when reconstructing Ystar = exp(lnZ_trend)·K^α; never swap K sources between derivation and reconstruction. (3) Add a mandatory sanity-check cell immediately below Ystar outputs: `=Ystar_lastHist / Y_observed_lastHist − 1`, formatted as %, yellow background. If |ratio| > 20% OR Ystar is off by ≥10× from Y_observed, STOP — units are wrong; do not proceed to projection. (4) For shock-analysis-supply specifically: Ystar_base in Production!H60:H65 must land in 10,000–500,000 (mn GEL); if it is in the tens or hundreds, the PWT→GEL conversion was omitted. (5) Keep unit tags in headers (e.g., `K (mn GEL, real 2017)`, `Y (mn GEL, real)`) and never combine two series whose header units differ without passing through a named conversion cell.
